commit.subject: fix(socks5): own peers and retain all handler failures
commit.author: Arya Alikhani <AryaAlikhani@icloud.com>

contract_repairs: Ordinary origin/proxy spawn immediately creates canonical ConnectionPeer before fallible client operations. Both listening addresses are acquired before paired tasks start.
Each real client operation returns Result into route cleanup, preserving the request failure as original primary and retaining simultaneous typed peer failures through existing finish_with_cleanup.
Raw controlled task handles explicitly become ConnectionPeer before helper future polling; seven call signatures now pass Ok(()) with owners. Their control observations and assertions are unchanged.

Route completion selects either peer; on failure it observes an already-completed sibling outcome or explicitly stops/awaits a live sibling. Completed cancellation/panic is retained before a fresh abort request.

Both authenticated origin acquisition and proxy-handler completion use one owner-local collector. A listener/TLS acquisition failure remains primary; completed outcomes are drained before abort; all live children receive requested cancellation and awaited bounded cleanup.
Collector ignores only cancellation after its own abort_all request, retains completed prior cancellation, panic/typed errors, and adds concrete typed contextual cleanup deadline on timeout.
Successful collector waits all handlers and preserves values/completion order; existing credential separation and HTTP2 connection path arrays remain literal.
Pool proxy JoinSet collector stays lexical so top-level cancellation cannot bypass its child cleanup by aborting an intermediate spawned collector.
Natural auth module declaration replaces redundant path attribute; imports now precede declarations. No shared API, production client, manifests or support source changed.
manual_layout_review: Manually reviewed setup, request/response and cleanup paragraphs of all changed owner callers, raw adoption call sites, completed-cause guards, collector wait/pre-abort/drain/deadline phases and concrete deadline type beside implementations. Existing control bodies/oracles intentionally preserved. No arbitrary size split or new framework.
